subject: history
title: Reconstruction to Jim Crow 1865-1900
welcome_lead: From the Thirteenth Amendment to Plessy v Ferguson: the long shadow of slavery.
meta_desc: A-Level history adventure on Reconstruction, Jim Crow and the failure of the post-Civil War settlement.

concepts.def: Ratified 6 December 1865 abolishing slavery throughout the United States.
Ratified 1868 granting citizenship and equal protection of the laws.
Ratified 1870 prohibiting denial of the vote on grounds of race or previous servitude.
Southern state laws after 1865 restricting freed people's rights and forcing them into labour contracts.
White-supremacist terror organisation founded in Tennessee in 1865 to intimidate Black voters.
1896 Supreme Court ruling establishing 'separate but equal', legitimising Jim Crow segregation.

walkthroughs.body_html: Congress overrode Andrew Johnson's vetoes to pass the 1867 Reconstruction Acts dividing the South into military districts and requiring Black male suffrage. Black men were elected to Congress; the Freedmen's Bureau provided schools. The 1877 Compromise withdrew federal troops, ending Reconstruction. Within decades white 'redeemer' governments rolled back voting rights through poll taxes and literacy tests.

Northern political will waned amid economic depression after 1873. Klan violence intimidated Black voters despite the 1870-71 Enforcement Acts. The Supreme Court narrowed civil rights protections (Slaughter-House Cases 1873, US v Cruikshank 1876). The 1877 Compromise traded Hayes's presidency for troop withdrawal. Eric Foner's classic study reframes Reconstruction as 'America's unfinished revolution'.

walkthroughs.h2: Plessy and the Jim Crow order
walkthroughs.body_html: Mississippi's 1890 constitution introduced literacy tests and grandfather clauses, reducing Black registration from 70 per cent to single digits. Plessy v Ferguson (1896) legitimised segregation. Lynchings averaged over 100 per year in the 1890s. Booker T. Washington's 1895 Atlanta Compromise accepted segregation in return for vocational uplift; W.E.B. Du Bois's Niagara Movement 1905 demanded full rights.

numericals.q: In which year did federal Reconstruction effectively end with the Compromise?
